notes: Six UBC Sauder "PhD in Business Administration / Alumni / <year>" pages (1997, 1998, 2002, 2004, 2005, 2007), two Common Crawl captures each (CC-MAIN-2017-47 and CC-MAIN-2018-47); the two captures of every page carry identical rows and the same "Last Updated on 9/20/2017" footer, so each person appears twice (once per snapshot). Year meaning: each page is titled "UBC PhD Alumni <year>" (or has a "<year>" section heading) and the 2004/2005/2007 pages open with "Since graduating its first student in 1972, the Sauder School of Business PhD Program has seen (over) 200 students proceed to academic, government, and industry positions"; the year list on the 2007 page runs 1972-2007. The page never states explicitly that the year is the graduation year, so yearMeaning is recorded as "unstated"; the integrator may reasonably read it as graduation year given the 1972 first-graduate statement, but that is an interpretation. destination is copied from the "Current University" column, i.e. the affiliation at page-update time (9/20/2017), NOT a stated first placement; some entries are industry employers (Royal Bank of Canada, Geomarkets.com, Inc., UBS Warburg). Division codes (MKT, FIN, MIS, SC, OB, POL, ACC, ULE, TLOG, SBE, INT, IB, TRA) are kept in note; "SC" and "TLOG" rows (Dongsheng Zhou 1997; R. Keith Freeland and Moren Levesque 1998; Xiaomei Ding and Greys Sosic 2002; Weon-Sang Yoo and Xuan Zhao 2004; Shuya Yin 2005; Xiaowen Fu 2007) are the likely operations/logistics-relevant graduates. Email addresses and personal-web-page links printed on the pages were deliberately not copied (personal contact details). Institution spellings are kept as written, including "MGill University, Montreal", "SeoGang University", "Beijing University", "Texas A & M International", and "California State University at Los Angeles" for a person whose email is on a csus.edu domain (emails omitted). No position titles are given on these pages. The 2004 page says "200 students"; the 2007 page says "over 200 students".
